dns.title: DNS
dns.intro: Connect Cloudflare, and this server makes each site's DNS record, and gets certificates checked through DNS, wildcards included.
dns.cloudflare.title: Cloudflare
dns.connect.intro: This server needs an API token from your Cloudflare account. Open Cloudflare, create the token there (everything is filled in), and paste it below.
dns.connect.howTo: How to make the token, step by step
dns.connect.step1: Select **Open Cloudflare**, and sign in if asked. Cloudflare's form opens with a name and the permissions below already filled in.
dns.connect.step2: Under **Zone Resources**, choose the domains this server handles, or keep **All zones**.
dns.connect.step3: Select **Continue to summary**, and check that it lists the three permissions below. If one is missing, select **Edit token** and add it. Then select **Create Token**.
dns.connect.step4: Copy the token Cloudflare shows (it shows it only once), and paste it below.
dns.connect.permDnsWhy: to make each site's DNS record, and to prove certificates through DNS
dns.cloudflare.stored: It is checked with Cloudflare, then stored encrypted and never shown again.
dns.cloudflare.removeConfirm: Remove the Cloudflare token? Records made with it stay in Cloudflare, but this server no longer changes them, and certificates checked through DNS can no longer be renewed.
dns.records.title: DNS records for sites
dns.records.hint: Each DNS record points a site's domain at this server. Only records this server made are ever changed or deleted; a name that already has a record made elsewhere is left alone.
dns.records.forEverySite: Give every site a DNS record
dns.records.forEverySiteHint: Made when a site is created, moved when the site changes domain, deleted with it. Existing sites get one too. You can also give single sites a record below.
dns.records.addressHint: This server's public address, or a host name such as a load balancer's. Not both.
dns.records.proxiedHint: Visitors go through Cloudflare (the orange cloud) and see Cloudflare's certificate. In Cloudflare, open the domain, then **SSL/TLS → Overview**, and choose **Full (strict)**. The sites then need a certificate Cloudflare trusts, chosen under **HTTPS** in the menu: Let's Encrypt or a Cloudflare Origin certificate.
dns.records.proxiedHintOutside: Visitors go through Cloudflare (the orange cloud) and see Cloudflare's certificate. In Cloudflare, open the domain, then **SSL/TLS → Overview**, and choose **Full (strict)**, so that Cloudflare checks the certificate of whatever handles HTTPS in front of this server.
dns.records.detectFailed: This server's public address could not be found. Type it in.
dns.records.saved: Saved. Records are brought up to date now.
dns.sites.title: Sites
dns.sites.removeConfirm: Delete the DNS records this server made for {domain}? Visitors stop reaching it by name once the change spreads. This server makes none for it again until you create one.
dns.site.added: The DNS record of {domain} is in place.
dns.site.removed: The DNS records of {domain} are deleted.
dns.state.excluded: deleted by hand: none is made again
dns.state.noZone: no zone the token can edit holds this domain
dns.state.conflict: a record made elsewhere is there ({records}), so this server leaves it alone
dns.error.tokenRefused: Cloudflare refused the token: {problem}. Make one with the steps above: an API token, not the Global API Key.
dns.error.noZones: The token cannot see any zone. Give it Zone: Read and DNS: Edit on your zones.
dns.error.notConnected: Connect Cloudflare first, with a token.
dns.error.targetAndAddress: Give addresses or a host name, not both.
dns.error.noAddress: Give an address or a host name for records to point at.
